metaDescription: Six digital kitchen scales compared on capacity, resolution, platform size, power and display, with picks for baking, meal prep, coffee and bulk cooking.
expertTake: The OXO Good Grips 11-pound scale is the best pick for everyday baking and cooking because of its pull-out display and clean design, and the Etekcity 11 lb scale is the value pick. Anyone weighing tiny amounts such as spices or coffee doses should skip the standard 1 g scales and look for finer resolution.
introParagraphs: A digital kitchen scale converts weight to a number so recipes become repeatable. It replaces cup measures, which vary a lot for flour and other dry goods, and makes portion tracking and meal prep far more consistent.

Capacity and resolution are the specs that matter, along with a platform large enough to hold a bowl and a display you can read around it. A scale that is accurate but hides its numbers under your mixing bowl is a poor fit for baking.

products.name: OXO Good Grips 11 pound digital kitchen scale with pull-out display
products.description:
The OXO Good Grips scale pairs an 11 pound capacity with a stainless steel platform and a display that pulls out of the base. The pull-out feature lifts the screen away from the platform so a large bowl does not cover the numbers, which is the most common irritation with flat scales. It converts between multiple units and has a zero function for removing the weight of a container.

The tradeoff is price and simplicity. Compared with the Etekcity 11 lb, it sits in a higher price tier for similar capacity, and compared with the 22 lb Greater Goods it holds half the weight. It uses a standard resolution of about one gram, so it is not the choice for micro measurements. For ordinary baking, portioning and general kitchen use, the readability is a genuine advantage.

In ownership, wipe the stainless platform with a damp cloth and avoid immersing the base. Replace the batteries when the display dims, since low power causes drift. Keep the pull-out display clean of flour, which can work its way into the slider.
products.bestFor: Home cooks and bakers who want an easy-to-read scale for everyday use.
pros: Pull-out display keeps the numbers visible beside a large mixing bowl
Stainless platform wipes clean and resists staining
Zero function makes adding ingredients one after another simple
Multi-unit conversion covers grams, ounces and pounds
cons: Higher price tier than other 11 lb scales for the same capacity
Standard one gram resolution is not enough for tiny measurements

products.name: Etekcity 11 lb digital kitchen scale in grams and ounces with tare

specList.label: Units

products.description:
The Etekcity 11 lb scale offers 5 kg of capacity, a resolution of one gram and five unit settings that include milliliters. The tare function lets you zero a bowl and weigh ingredients one at a time. It is among the lower price tiers in the lineup and is the baseline scale for most home kitchens.

The tradeoff is feel and display. Compared with the OXO, it has a flat display that a bowl can cover, and compared with the Greater Goods 22 lb it is limited to 11 pounds, which is fine for baking but low for bulk meal prep. Against the Etekcity 22 lb USB model, it is simpler and uses disposable batteries. It is a sound choice if you want accuracy without extras.

For care, wipe the platform with a damp cloth and keep it dry. Replace the batteries when the readings start to wander or the screen dims. Place the scale on a hard, flat counter for consistent results, since soft surfaces can skew readings.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a dependable everyday baking and cooking scale.

products.name: Escali Primo digital food scale with two-button operation
products.description:
The Escali Primo is a compact digital food scale that uses just two buttons, one for power and tare and one for unit conversion. It is built for people who want a scale with nothing to learn and a small footprint that fits in a drawer. It has a long history in home baking and is a straightforward choice for cooks who prefer minimal controls.

The tradeoff is that simplicity limits capacity and features. Compared with the OXO, it has no pull-out display, and compared with the Greater Goods it is not built for heavy loads. Against the Etekcity 11 lb, it is similar in capability but comes with a more established brand name and a slightly higher price tier. It is a good fit for baking and portioning rather than bulk prep.

Care is minimal. Wipe the surface, keep it away from steam and replace the batteries when needed. Check the zero reading with an empty platform every few weeks, and avoid putting heavy pans on a scale rated for light loads.

products.name: Greater Goods 22 lb digital food scale with stainless platform
products.description:
The Greater Goods scale raises capacity to 22 pounds while keeping a stainless steel platform and a high-definition LCD display. The higher limit helps when weighing a full bowl of dough, a large batch of meal prep or a big package of meat. It is built for bulk cooking rather than precision micro measurements.

The tradeoff is that higher capacity usually means coarser resolution on the low end. Compared with the OXO, it can weigh twice as much but has no pull-out screen, and against the Etekcity 22 lb it lacks rechargeable power and an IPX6 rating. It is a good fit for batch cooks, home butchers and anyone who regularly fills a big mixing bowl.

In ownership, keep the platform clean and avoid overloading it. Replace batteries promptly and place it on a hard surface. Check the reading against a known weight, such as a sealed pack of known size, now and then.

products.name: Etekcity 22 lb USB rechargeable food scale with IPX6 waterproof design
products.description:
The Etekcity 22 lb scale adds USB charging and an IPX6 waterproof rating to a 10 kg capacity and one gram resolution. IPX6 means it can handle powerful water jets, so a splash or a rinse is not a problem. Rechargeable power removes the disposable battery cycle, which is the most common long-term nuisance with kitchen scales.

The tradeoff is complexity and price. Compared with the Etekcity 11 lb, it costs more and the built-in battery can eventually fade. Against the Greater Goods, it adds charging and waterproofing but lacks a pull-out display. It suits people who wash their scale often and want a long-running, low-maintenance machine.

Ownership tips: charge the unit when the display dims, rinse it gently rather than submerging it and dry it before storage. Keep the charging port covered or dry, since moisture there is the likeliest failure point.

pros: IPX6 waterproofing makes cleanup after messy jobs easy
USB charging avoids repeated battery purchases

cons: Higher price tier than basic 11 lb scales

products.name: KUAIVO dual platform kitchen scale with two precisions and 33 lb capacity
products.description:
The KUAIVO scale has two weighing platforms, one for large loads up to 33 pounds and one with much finer resolution, down to 0.001 ounce, for small amounts. It offers seven units and a tare function. This is the one design here that tries to cover both bulk cooking and micro measurements such as spices, coffee or supplements.

The tradeoff is that a dual platform needs more space and more care. Compared with the OXO, it has a more confusing layout, and compared with the Greater Goods it is an unknown brand with less long-term owner history. The fine platform is useful but fragile, and the stated resolution is not the same as proven accuracy. Treat it as a flexible helper rather than a lab instrument.

For care, never overload the fine platform, and keep both clean and dry. Zero the scale before each use, and recheck against a known weight every few months to see if either platform has drifted.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Capacity ranges from 11 lb on the OXO and Etekcity 11 lb to 22 lb on the Greater Goods and 33 lb on the KUAIVO. A mixing bowl and dough can weigh several pounds, so leave headroom. Buyers often pick a scale rated just above their heaviest load, then overload it in practice, which causes error messages and drift.

Most scales here read in 1 g steps, enough for flour, sugar and meal portions. The KUAIVO fine platform reads to 0.001 oz, which suits spices or coffee. Resolution is the smallest step displayed, not how accurate the weight is, so a fine display on a cheap sensor can still be wrong by a gram or more.

A small platform fits only a small bowl, while a large one dominates the counter. The OXO pull-out display solves the problem of a bowl blocking the numbers. Look at the platform size and the screen position, because bowl diameter and sightline matter as much as the sensor.

Disposable batteries in the Etekcity 11 lb, OXO and Escali are easy to replace but need attention, since low power makes readings wander. USB rechargeable scales such as the Etekcity 22 lb avoid disposable cells but have a built-in battery that eventually fades. Pick the option you will remember to maintain.

Tare zeroes a bowl so you can weigh ingredients in sequence. Units range from five on the Etekcity 11 lb to seven on the KUAIVO. Many scales offer milliliters, but that conversion assumes water-like density, so it is unreliable for oil or honey.

Flour, dough and spills reach the platform quickly. The Etekcity 22 lb carries an IPX6 rating, while the others are splash-resistant at best. A smooth platform and sealed buttons make cleanup faster and reduce long-term failures.

specDecoder.meaning: Capacity is the maximum weight the scale can read, such as 11 lb or 22 lb. Going past it can cause errors or damage the sensor.
specDecoder.watchFor: Add the weight of your largest bowl to your heaviest ingredient before choosing.

specDecoder.meaning: Resolution is the smallest step the display shows, usually 1 g, or 0.001 oz on the KUAIVO fine platform. It affects how finely you can measure small amounts.
specDecoder.watchFor: Higher resolution does not equal higher accuracy, so be cautious with very fine claims.

specDecoder.meaning: Tare resets the display to zero with a container on the platform. It lets you add ingredients one by one without math.
specDecoder.watchFor: All scales here have tare, but check that it works smoothly with heavy bowls.

specDecoder.meaning: An IPX rating shows protection against water. IPX6 on the Etekcity 22 lb means it can handle strong water jets, though not submersion.
specDecoder.watchFor: Most other scales in this guide list no rating, so keep them dry.

specDecoder.meaning: Unit conversion switches between grams, ounces, pounds and milliliters. Milliliters are only accurate for liquids with water-like density.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not trust milliliter conversion for oil, syrup or milk without checking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and resolution
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared capacities from 11 lb to 33 lb and resolutions from 1 g to 0.001 oz on the KUAIVO fine platform. We weighed whether each figure matches real kitchen tasks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Display and usability
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how readable each display is with a bowl on the platform. The OXO pull-out screen scored well here, while flat designs lost points when a large bowl blocks them.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at battery type and long-term ownership, including the Etekcity 22 lb rechargeable battery and the IPX6 rating. Owners often cite battery drift and water damage as the common failures.

maintenance.why: Flour and oil build up on the platform and can reach the sensor edges. A damp cloth keeps readings reliable.
Low power causes drift and random reboots. Fresh cells or a full charge restore stability.
An empty platform should read zero. If it does not, tare it and check for debris under the edges.
A sealed pack with a printed weight shows whether the scale is off. Replace a scale that drifts by several grams.
Stacking heavy pans on a scale can damage the sensors. Keep the scale in a dry spot away from steam.

faq.q: Do I need a 22 lb scale instead of 11 lb?
faq.a: Only if you regularly weigh large bowls of dough, bulk meat or meal prep batches. For most baking and portioning, an 11 lb scale such as the OXO or Etekcity 11 lb has plenty of headroom.

faq.q: Is a more expensive kitchen scale more accurate?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Price often buys build quality, display design and features. A well-made scale with 1 g resolution is accurate enough for nearly all home recipes.

faq.q: How long do kitchen scales last?
faq.a: With dry storage and fresh power, several years is typical. Owner feedback patterns show failures from water damage, overloading and corroded battery contacts.
Only if the sensor and platform support it. The KUAIVO fine platform reads to that step, but real accuracy depends on build quality, so treat extremely fine figures with caution.

faq.q: Can I trust the milliliter setting?
faq.a: Only for water-like liquids such as milk. Oil, honey and syrup have different densities, so a milliliter reading from a scale will be off for them.

faq.q: Can I weigh hot items on a scale?
faq.a: Avoid very hot pans on a scale, because heat can damage the platform and sensor. Let items cool a little, or place a trivet on the platform and tare it first.
